headline: The AI complex is now the funding source: a +1.6% S&P and a +3.0% Dow built entirely on liquidating power, chips and energy into consumers, housing and gold miners.
summary: Yesterday was a dollar-and-vol story. Today it is a forced factor unwind dressed up as a rally. SPX +1.6% to 7688.6, DJI +3.0%, equal-weight RSP +1.9% — but NDX only +0.9% and QQQ/SPY fell another 0.7% to z=-3.03 with acceleration z=-3.27. Under the index: XLY +4.3%, XLF +3.5%, XLP +3.4%, XLRE +3.3%, XLV +3.1%, versus XLE -4.7% and XLK flat. ITB +7.2%, XHB +5.4%, XRT +5.5%, JETS +6.7%, IHI +6.7%, HD +6.5% (z=3.70, acc 3.96), MCD +6.5% (z=3.98), DHI +8.1%, WMT +22.9% on the month. RSP/SPY sits at z=+3.45 with acceleration +3.67; high-beta/low-vol is -20.9% on the month at z=-3.26 and growth/value is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. This is the widest, most violent rotation in the dataset, and it is happening on an up day for the index — which is why it has gone largely unpunished so far.

The epicenter moved. Last week it was semis; today it is everything that monetizes AI capex downstream. VST -13.8% (21.2% below its 200-day, 0th percentile of the year), ETN -9.9% (-18.4% on the month, z=-2.64), GEV -9.3%, CEG -6.7%, GRID -3.1% and -10.9% on the month at z=-2.04, NLR at the 0th percentile. Chips kept bleeding into it: SOXX -3.1% and -23.6% on the month at z=-2.62, SMH/SPY z=-3.23, MU -7.0% (-25.2% on the month), ASML -3.6%, NVDA -3.2%. Asia took the clearing price — KOSPI -5.3% in a session that required a program-trading sidecar halt, and -22.4% on the month at z=-3.04 and 18.0% below its 200-day; TAIEX -3.2%, Nikkei -1.8%. Meanwhile the non-chip mega-caps were the bid: MSFT +6.7% (52-week high, 26.9% above its 200-day), AAPL +5.3%, AMZN +6.1%, GOOGL +3.2% off a -16.6% month. Software over semis is now a trend, not a wobble: IGV/SMH +3.7% today, +18.6% on the month, z=2.64 and turning up.

Two of yesterday's open gaps closed in a single session. The gold miners finally caught the metal: GDX +9.0%, GDXJ +9.6%, NEM +9.9% against gold +1.5% to 4132.9, with GDX/gold +5.1% and turning up. And energy equity finally capitulated to crude — XLE -4.7%, XOP -6.4%, OIH -4.9%, XOM -4.6%, CVX -3.7% on a day WTI rose 1.3% to 89.29 and Brent 2.2%. That is the gap trade paying off, not a new entry; XLE is still 8.8% above its 200-day. The rates backdrop remains the quiet support: 10-year -5bp to 4.90 and -41bp on the month, 5-year -37bp, 30-year 5.28%, 10-year real yield 2.64%, and MOVE -6.1% to 93.88, now -17.4% on the month. Credit held: HYG +0.7%, LQD +0.8%, BKLN at the 100th percentile of its year, credit & vol composite at +12 versus -31 yesterday. Risk regime improved to -5 from -14.

What should worry you is the price of insurance against all this. VIX is 16.93 at the 19.7th percentile of the year, VIX3M fell 11.6%, term structure 0.88 — index vol is priced for calm while single-stock dispersion is at historic extremes and SKEW is 150.9 and turning up with acceleration 1.03. The duration rally is also stretched, not trending: TLT is +6.0% on the month at z=1.64 with acceleration 2.12 yet still 2.1% below its 200-day; 3m10y has collapsed 40bp on the month to 0.69 because bills won't move (3m 4.21, unchanged); 10-year breakevens are 2.26 at the 25th percentile while the CPI index is up 106bp year-to-date and the 30-year mortgage is stuck at 7.24%. And LatAm is still broken independent of the dollar: USDBRL +9.0% on the month at z=2.61, EWZ -25.0% at z=-3.32, Bovespa z=-3.77 with acceleration -4.05, EEM/SPY z=-2.30.

good.text: Bond volatility is gone: MOVE -6.1% to 93.88, -17.4% on the month, while 10s fell 5bp to 4.90 and are -41bp on the month and 5s -37bp. The rates composite improved to -28 from -33 and credit & vol flipped to +12 from -31.
Breadth is the best in the dataset's history: RSP/SPY z=+3.45 with acceleration +3.67, equal-weight S&P +5.8% on the month at the 100th percentile, Dow +3.0% on the day, RUT +1.6% and turning up.
Credit refuses to crack through an equity-internals bloodbath: HYG +0.7%, LQD +0.8%, BKLN at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range, HYG/IEF turning up off z=-1.69.

The rate-sensitive consumer is being bought aggressively: ITB +7.2% (+17.2% on the month), XHB +5.4%, XRT +5.5% (+13.0%), HD +6.5% at z=3.70, MCD +6.5% at z=3.98, DHI +8.1%. XHB/SPY z=2.38, XRT/SPY z=2.85.
Gold miners finally closed the discount to the metal — GDX +9.0%, GDXJ +9.6%, NEM +9.9% versus gold +1.5% — with GDX/gold +5.1% and turning up. Yesterday's stranded equity is no longer stranded.

Europe and the China/India complex are the clean side of the world: DAX +4.6% on the month at the 100th percentile, FTSE at the 100th, HSI +3.7% and KWEB +4.5% on the day, Sensex +2.6% (+8.5% on the month, z=2.00), INDA +2.7%.

bad.text: The AI-power and electrification trade is being liquidated at speed, and the acceleration is bearish: VST -13.8% and 21.2% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile, ETN -9.9% (z=-2.64), GEV -9.3%, CEG -6.7%, GRID -10.9% on the month at z=-2.04, NLR at the 0th percentile.

Asian semis are in a disorderly unwind: KOSPI -5.3% in one session (sidecar halt) and -22.4% on the month at z=-3.04, TAIEX -3.2% at z=-3.13, SOXX -23.6% on the month, MU -7.0%, ASML -3.6%, TSM -2.2%, SMH/SPY z=-3.23.

Momentum and growth are being destroyed, not rotated: MTUM -15.6% on the month at z=-2.91, high-beta/low-vol -20.9% at z=-3.26, growth/value at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, QQQ/SPY z=-3.03 with acceleration -3.27.

Index vol is mispriced against this dispersion: VIX 16.93 at the 19.7th percentile, VIX3M -11.6%, term structure 0.88, but SKEW 150.9 turning up with acceleration 1.03. Protection is cheap because nobody needs it on an up day.

Energy equity capitulated into a rising crude tape — XLE -4.7%, XOP -6.4%, OIH -4.9%, XOM -4.6%, CVX -3.7% while WTI rose 1.3% and Brent 2.2%. The gap closed violently; XLE is still 8.8% above its 200-day, so it isn't finished.
Brazil is a local credit event, not dollar beta: USDBRL +9.0% on the month at z=2.61 even with DXY flat, EWZ -25.0% at z=-3.32, Bovespa acceleration z=-4.05. EM/US is z=-2.30 and rolling over.

trades.name: Short the AI power/electrification complex
trades.line: Short VST/GEV/ETN basket: AI capex derivative is breaking
trades.expr: Equal-weight short VST, GEV, ETN, CEG (25% each); or buy Jan put spreads 10-15% OTM in VST and GEV. Hedge 30% of notional with long XLU to isolate the AI-capex component.
trades.thesis: The chips cracked first; the downstream monetizers of AI capex are now repricing with a lag and from far higher relative valuations. These are crowded 2025-26 momentum vehicles with no index-level support, and the rotation out of AI is feeding them to the bid in consumer and healthcare.
trades.trigger: VST -13.8% in a session to 21.2% below its 200-day at the 0th percentile of the year; ETN -9.9% and -18.4% on the month at z=-2.64 with acceleration -2.04; GEV -9.3%; CEG -6.7%; GRID -10.9% on the month at z=-2.04, rolling over; NLR -14.9% on the month, 0th percentile.
trades.stop: GRID reclaims its 200-day (currently -8.9%) or SMH/SPY turns up off z=-3.23 with NVDA back above its 200-day — that means the capex scare is over and these snap hardest.
trades.target: Another 15-20% in the basket; VST toward 100, GRID toward 145.

trades.name: Long software vs short semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH: ratio breaking out, still 40th pctile
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral long IGV vs short SMH, 1:1 notional. Add a small long IGV call overlay for convexity.
trades.thesis: Software monetizes AI without carrying the capital intensity; semis carry the balance sheet. The ratio collapsed 35.5% over a year and is only now mean-reverting — it is up 18.6% on the month and still sits at the 40th percentile of its 52-week range, so there is runway without needing a new narrative.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +3.7% today, +18.6% on the month at z=2.64 with acceleration 2.26, turning up. SOXX -23.6% on the month at z=-2.62; SMH -20.4%; IGV holds 10.1% above its 200-day with a turning-up relative-strength state.
trades.stop: Ratio back below 0.190 (-7.5% from 0.2054), or MU and TSM both reclaim their 200-day.

trades.name: Buy index downside while it's cheap
trades.line: Dec SPX put spreads / VIX call spreads with VIX at 16.9
trades.expr: Buy Dec SPX 5% OTM / 12% OTM put spreads, roughly 1.5% of NAV premium; or VIX Dec 20/30 call spreads. Sell a 3% OTM Dec call against it if you need to cheapen carry.
trades.thesis: The index is masking a violent internal liquidation. Realized dispersion like this — high-beta/low-vol -20.9% in a month, momentum -15.6%, Korea -22.4% — historically resolves through an index-level air pocket when the long leg (consumer, staples, healthcare) finally gets taken as the source of funds.
trades.trigger: VIX 16.93 at the 19.7th percentile of its 52-week range and VIX3M down 11.6% to 18.80 (11.6th percentile) on the same day SKEW rose to 150.9 and turned up with acceleration 1.03. Tail demand is rising while at-the-money vol is being sold.
trades.stop: VIX3M sustained below 17 with SKEW back under 145 and RSP/SPY acceleration fading — that is an orderly broadening, not a liquidation.

trades.name: Long Germany/UK vs short Korea
trades.line: Long EWG+EWU / short EWY: capex beta vs domestic earnings
trades.expr: Long 50% EWG + 50% EWU vs short EWY, equal notional, FX unhedged.
trades.thesis: Korea is the purest listed proxy for AI memory capex and is unwinding with circuit breakers; Germany and the UK are domestic-earnings markets making 52-week highs with falling global yields and a soft dollar. The pair is long the rotation's destination and short its source.
trades.trigger: KOSPI -5.3% in a session, -22.4% on the month at z=-3.04 and 18.0% below its 200-day; EWY -20.5% on the month. Against that, DAX +4.6% on the month at the 100th percentile, FTSE at the 100th, EWG +3.4% and EWU +3.4% today, EFA/SPY +2.7% on the month with acceleration 1.99.
trades.stop: Pair drawdown of 6%, or EWY reclaiming its 200-day (currently -6.7% away).

trades.name: Long gold miners vs the metal
trades.line: Long GDX / short GLD: the equity discount is finally closing
trades.expr: Long GDX (add 25% GDXJ and a GDX Jan 90 call overlay) vs short GLD at ~0.6x notional to neutralize bullion beta.
trades.thesis: Miners spent the entire gold drawdown trading worse than the metal; that discount is now unwinding with the metal stabilizing. Operating leverage works in both directions and the ratio has barely started.
trades.trigger: GDX +9.0%, GDXJ +9.6%, NEM +9.9% against gold +1.5% to 4132.9; GDX/gold +5.1% on the day and turning up with acceleration 0.46. GDX is still 6.4% below its 200-day at the 35th percentile while the ratio sits at the 66th — the equity has room the metal does not.
trades.stop: GDX/gold back below 0.215 (-5%), or gold losing 4000 with silver failing to hold 50.

trades.name: Fade the stretched duration rally
trades.line: Short TLT: 41bp of 10y rally with acc z=-2.61 is stretched
trades.expr: Short TLT, or buy Dec/Jan TLT 80 puts; alternatively short IEF outright. Size for a 10bp adverse move in 10s.
trades.thesis: This is a positioning rally, not a repricing of the Fed. Bills haven't moved, so the entire move is term structure compression into a curve that is already too flat to keep going. With breakevens at the 25th percentile and the CPI index up 106bp year-to-date, the disinflation leg is largely priced.
trades.trigger: 10s -41bp on the month with acceleration z=-2.61, 5s acceleration -2.31, TLT +6.0% at z=1.64 with acceleration 2.12 yet still 2.1% below its 200-day in a downtrend; 3m10y collapsed 40bp to 0.69 with the 3-month bill unchanged at 4.21; 2s10s down to 0.32 at the 22nd percentile; 30-year mortgage still 7.24% and +21bp on the month.
trades.stop: TLT above 85 or 10-year yield through 4.65 — that is a growth scare and the thesis is wrong.
